R01.mechanism_target: completion claims in agent reports vs `git log`/`git status`
R01.observed_prior_facts: the agent's final report text (subagentstop payload) plus whether a git status/log verification ran before the claim was relayed — tool-event history
R01.reason: No single artifact decides it (a completion claim is phrased many ways); the violation is a sequence — a 'committed' claim relayed without a subsequent repo check, both facts visible in hook payloads and the event history.

R02.observed_prior_facts: a prior `git push` Bash event and the presence/absence of a Playwright live-URL check event between the push and the announcement
R02.reason: Compliance hinges on ordering — push happened, live-URL verification did or did not run before the 'it is live' claim — which is event history, not a pattern in one artifact.

R03.cost: Reference documentation of an adopted corpus and how to query it; there is no behavior to comply with, so any check would have nothing to decide.
R03.importance: בינונית — useful orientation material for planning work, but it prescribes nothing enforceable.
R03.reason: Documentation/historical record of where the thinking-models material came from and how to read it — no compliance condition.

R04.observed_prior_facts: the count of currently-running agents and whether a suite run/build/GPU queue is active — derivable from agent start/stop events and process state in the state store
R04.reason: A single dispatch payload cannot decide compliance; the decision needs a counter of concurrent agents and knowledge of active heavy processes, i.e. prior events.

R05.reason: Whether a rendered string is correct Hebrew — right singular/plural on interpolated counts, right domain term, no leak — requires linguistic and domain judgment of the content, not a nameable textual pattern.

R06.reason: Both gates trigger on a judged situation ('identical-looking code behaves differently', 'was the scripted edit verified by running it') — recognizing the situation and the adequacy of the verification requires evaluating meaning, not matching a pattern.

R07.reason: Whether a plan identified the hardest constraint first, is MECE at requirement level, or weighed reversibility is a quality judgment over the plan's content — no artifact pattern decides it.

R08.reason: Deciding that a plan 'waives, defers, or reinterprets' an approved spec requirement means comparing the meaning of plan text against spec text; words like 'deferred' appear legitimately, so no lexical pattern is decisive.

R09.reason: 'Prove the probe actually ran the workload before reasoning from a surprising measurement' requires judging whether evidence supports a conclusion — an assessment of meaning, not a pattern in an artifact.

R10.mechanism_target: test runs vs edits (RED-before-GREEN) and full-suite runs after each task close
R10.observed_prior_facts: the ordered history of test executions (with failing then passing outcomes) relative to code edits, and whether `npx playwright test` ran after each task — all in the tool-event history
R10.reason: Both extracted gates are sequence conditions — a RED run observed before implementation, a whole-suite run after every task — decidable from prior events, not from any single artifact.

R11.artifact: the brief file passed at agent dispatch (template docs/process/templates/task-brief.md), visible in the pretooluse:Agent payload
R11.pattern: presence/absence of the required brief sections — quoted spec lines, exact plan code, DoD checklist, report contract including the H9 table requirement, and a primary-tool field; a missing or placeholder section (e.g. 'TODO') is the violation
R11.mechanism_target: task-brief files under the brief/report contract
R11.reason: The brief contract is a fixed template whose required fields are structurally checkable before dispatch — the text itself says a missing field = an invalid brief and that check-brief already rejects slices.

R12.observed_prior_facts: whether a rendered-DOM-per-language measurement (Playwright run against the built app) exists in the event history before the coverage claim is stated
R12.reason: The gate is an ordering condition — a coverage claim is permitted only after a rendered-DOM measurement ran; that prior fact lives in the tool-event history, not in any pattern of the claim itself.

R13.cost: It is a one-line lessons-log record ('root cause X — gate: DoD 5') pointing at a gate that lives elsewhere; enforcing 'every derived value has a real, firing consumer' here would require runtime judgment the record itself does not define.
R13.importance: בינונית — the failure it records is real, but the operative compliance condition is DoD line 5, not this record.
R13.reason: Historical lesson record whose compliance condition is carried by another rule (DoD 5); on its own it states no checkable condition.

R14.reason: Detecting pre-judged reviewers, a test 'narrowed to fit the implementation', or the adequacy of two verdicts requires evaluating the meaning of briefs, tests and review content — judgment, not pattern.

R15.mechanism_target: implementation edits on items whose ledger row (docs/ROADMAP-2026-07-30.md §5a) is still ⚠️R
R15.observed_prior_facts: the ledger row's status and the presence/absence of a recorded owner verdict (בצע/בטל/R-cancelled) at the moment implementation work starts — read from the ledger document as state
R15.reason: The violation is ordering — implementation before the recorded owner decision on an ⚠️R item; deciding it needs the prior state of the ledger row relative to when work began, not a pattern in one artifact.

R16.reason: 'Repeatedly causes trouble' and 'genuinely better alternative was weighed' require attributing failures to a component and judging the quality of an evaluation — meaning and intent, not pattern or counter alone.

R17.artifact: the task-close report (subagentstop payload / the .superpowers/sdd report file) and the diff of docs/STATUS-BOARD.md
R17.pattern: presence of the fixed five H9 row headers — 'מה היה', 'מה נעשה', 'מה נשאר', 'איפה אנחנו', 'הבא בתור' — plus a ledger number in row 4, and a same-task update touching docs/STATUS-BOARD.md; absence of any of these is the violation
R17.reason: H9 mandates a fixed-format table with fixed row labels at every task end — a concrete structural pattern whose absence in the report decides non-compliance without reading intent.

R18.reason: Whether the controller did 'work a subagent could do' requires judging delegability of each piece of work — an evaluation of the work's nature, not any pattern or prior fact.

R19.reason: The entire rule turns on classifying a decision as 'important' vs 'routine' — hard to reverse, safety-relevant, owner-preference — which is an assessment of meaning and consequence.

R20.artifact: the Bash command in the pretooluse:Bash payload (plus the hook's known cwd)
R20.pattern: a command segment invoking a nested model process — leading word `claude` with `-p` — while the working directory is inside this repo / without an explicit cd to a neutral absolute path
R20.reason: The one kept gate ('run nested extraction from a NEUTRAL cwd, absolute paths') is decided by a concrete textual pattern in the shell command plus its cwd — no intent-reading needed; the rest of the section is explicitly historical.
